topics.topic: Whether assignment handling is limited to the single returned assignment or requires repository access to all assignments for the pair
questions: Must the note be limited to the single assignment returned by get_staff_assignment, or must the repository contract provide all assignments for the pair so the function can determine that every earlier assignment is revoked and preserve each one?

Must the requirement be limited to the single assignment returned by get_staff_assignment, or must the repository contract provide a way to read all assignments for the pair so the function can establish that they are all revoked and preserve each one?

Which passage must change: must the repository expose all assignments for the pair so assign_staff_project can establish that they are all revoked, or must the requirement be expressed in terms of the single assignment returned by get_staff_assignment?

quotes: assign_staff_project: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST make its own reads and writes, wherever its other notes call for them, of the records the StaffAccessRepository holds through get_staff of the staff_access repository of that transaction, and through its get_staff_assignment and its insert_staff_assignment.

assign_staff_project: [BEHAVIOR] MUST give a pair whose earlier assignments are all revoked a new assignment, built and inserted exactly as for a pair that never had one, and MUST leave every revoked assignment of the pair unchanged; it never updates or reactivates an earlier record.

assign_staff_project: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST inspect the validation result it receives for the project rather than discarding it: a project the Registry does not know is ScopedNotFoundError and a project it knows but reports as not active is ArchivedProjectRejected, both raised before the transaction opens, because an archived or unknown project accepts no mutation. An unknown operator_id is ScopedNotFoundError, and an operator that already holds an active assignment for that project is AuthorizationRejected.
judgement.why: The prompt explicitly limits repository access to the singular get_staff_assignment operation, uses it to detect an active duplicate, and preserves all revoked assignments by never updating or reactivating them, so enumeration of every historical assignment is not required.

questions: Which requirement must change: must grant_viewer_project read all grants for the pair through an operation such as list_viewer_grants so it can establish that all earlier grants are revoked, or must the new behavior be limited to the single ProjectViewerGrant | None returned by get_viewer_grant?

Which passage must change: must grant_viewer_project be allowed to read all grants for the viewer so it can establish that every earlier grant for the pair is revoked, or must the new behavior be stated only in terms of the single grant returned by get_viewer_grant?

quotes: grant_viewer_project: [BEHAVIOR] MUST give a pair whose earlier grants are all revoked a new grant, built and inserted exactly as for a pair that never had one, and MUST leave every revoked grant of the pair unchanged; it never updates or reactivates an earlier record.

grant_viewer_project: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST make its own reads and writes, wherever its other notes call for them, of the records the ViewerAccessRepository holds through get_viewer of the viewer_access repository of that transaction, and through its get_viewer_grant and its insert_viewer_grant.
judgement.why: The all-prior-grants condition is explicit, list_viewer_grants is an available repository operation, and the dependency note requires the named operations without saying they are the only repository operations permitted, so grant_viewer_project may additionally list grants to establish the condition.

topics.topic: Whether the repository must expose all grants for the pair or the behavior must cover only the single grant returned by get_producer_grant
questions: Which passage must change: must the repository expose a collection operation that lets the function establish that all earlier grants are revoked, or must the new note be limited to the single grant returned by get_producer_grant?

Which passage must change: must the repository expose all grants for the pair so the function can establish that they are all revoked, or must the behavior be stated only in terms of the single grant returned by get_producer_grant?

Must the repository contract provide all grants for the pair so the function can determine that they are all revoked and leave each unchanged, or must the note refer to the single grant returned by get_producer_grant?

quotes: grant_producer_project: [BEHAVIOR] MUST give a pair whose earlier grants are all revoked a new grant, built and inserted exactly as for a pair that never had one, and MUST leave every revoked grant of the pair unchanged; it never updates or reactivates an earlier record.

grant_producer_project: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST make its own reads and writes, wherever its other notes call for them, of the records the ServiceIdentityRepository holds through get_producer_grant of the service_identity repository of that transaction, and through its get_service_principal and its insert_producer_grant.
def get_producer_grant(self, principal_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> ProducerProjectGrant | None
judgement.why: The behavior requires establishing a predicate over every earlier grant and preserving each revoked record, while the mandatory repository read surface returns at most one grant for the pair, so an admissible history containing multiple grants cannot satisfy both obligations without either a collection operation or narrowing the behavior to the single returned grant.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
